blessedBy.note: The checker whose output these expectations were recorded from. NOT a gate — replaying against a candidate checker is the whole point — but a FAIL is only readable if you know what moved.

note: Recorded outcomes of the REAL validator (bakeoff parseSuiteManifest + collectManifestProblems) over recorded artefacts. expectFields are NORMALISED field paths (array indices collapsed, see signature.mjs). A field that disappears from the list is a FAILURE: the validator stopped naming something it used to name. A field that appears is DRIFT: reported, not fatal, because a validator that surveys more is the direction the 2026-08-10 repair round moved in.

cases.why: authoring attempt 1 of run-2026-08-09T21-04-00-713Z-a913c871. Emitted {entity, source, expectation} — no id, no kind, no minRows. Killed nothing on its own; it is the start of the id->kind->id oscillation.
cases.expectFailFastMessage: dataExpectations[0].id must be a non-empty string

cases.why: attempt 2. Told 'set dataExpectations[0].id', it added id and kept everything else wrong: {id, description, entity, minRowCount, readBack}.
cases.expectFailFastMessage: dataExpectations[0].kind must be "sqlite" or "http", got undefined

cases.why: attempt 3, THE MANIFEST THAT ENDED THE RUN. Told to add kind, it added kind and threw away the id it had right on attempt 2. docs/RUN-a913c871-observations.md records this exact case measured from the shipped bakeoff/dist: fail-fast names 1 field, collect-all names id | file | minRows | sql | table. That published measurement is this corpus's wiring proof — it was produced by a different reader on a different day.
cases.expectFailFastMessage: dataExpectations[0].id must be a non-empty string

cases.why: MUST-ACCEPT. A server-shaped manifest carrying the bakeoff/docker/README.md:391 sqlite entry verbatim plus an http entry. Without a must-accept case the whole corpus passes against a validator that rejects everything, which is the exact defect this repo catalogues twenty-one times.

MUST-ACCEPT, and it is the a913c871 root cause turned into a standing check: the dataExpectations examples the SHIPPED authoring prompt shows the seat, parsed by the real validator. A prompt that documents a shape the validator rejects puts the seat back in a box with no door it can see. Read from bakeoff/dist/spec-agent.js, so it tracks what a run would actually send.
